Apify web-search and web-fetch 2026-11-11 of official sources listed in each fact

facts.claim: Santa Marina's own 'Weddings & Celebrations' page (live, modified 23 October 2026) says the resort sits 'on the pristine shores of Mykonos', that its venues have 'scenic panoramas of the Aegean Sea', and that it has a 'traditional whitewashed stone chapel'. Re-check of Greece venues pack fact_10, fact_11: unchanged in substance.

Santa Marina says its 'experienced team of wedding planners' works with couples on intimate gatherings or grand celebrations, including bespoke menus, floral arrangements and elopement parties, and publishes a 2026 wedding brochure PDF and event menus PDF. Capacity, room count and exclusive use are not stated on the page read.

Santa Marina's site navigation lists Rooms, Suites and Villas, Santa Marina Beach, Oasis Pool, Buddha-Bar Beach Mykonos, Elais Restaurant, Private Dining and Ginkgo Spa; bookings run through Marriott (property code JMKLC), as a Luxury Collection resort.

Mykonos Grand Hotel & Resort describes itself as a five-star beachfront hotel on Ayios Yiannis (Agios Ioannis) beach, opposite the island of Delos, a member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World, with a private beach section reserved for hotel guests. Its home page meta description mentions 'Cycladic charm'.

Mykonos Grand's weddings page says its whitewashed chapel dedicated to the Virgin Mary is 'perched on a hill looking out over Ayios Yiannis Beach'; it holds up to 25 guests indoors and serves as a backdrop for outdoor ceremonies for up to 100 guests. The hotel will liaise with the couple's wedding planner and arranges music, video and photography, beauty salon services and flowers.

Mykonos Grand states that both bride and groom must be Christian Orthodox to perform a (religious) wedding within the hotel premises. Its amenity list also names an open-air amphitheatre and a complimentary evening shuttle to Mykonos Town. Accommodation includes rooms, suites with private pools and the Mykonos Grand Villa; total room count and exclusive use are not stated on the pages read.

Belvedere Hotel's home page places it on the edge of Mykonos Town near Rohari Hill, opposite the School of Fine Arts; it is a member of The Leading Hotels of the World with 31 rooms, 9 suites and 1 Mansion in the main hotel, plus a Waterfront Villa, Villa Next Door and 26 Hilltop Rooms and Suites about 250 m away. It says it is 'designed on the principle of a Cycladic neighbourhood'. The home page does not mention weddings.

Belvedere Hotel's contact page lists a 'Private Events' contact alongside reservations and guest relations, but neither the home page nor the contact page says the hotel hosts weddings, and a site-restricted search of belvederehotel.com for weddings or events returned no weddings page (only an events archive of restaurant openings and its historic White Parties). Belvedere does not meet the inclusion rule on this check.

Katikies Hotels' group events page says that across its Santorini and Mykonos hotels it creates bespoke events 'whether it's a lavish wedding, or a corporate event', lists Weddings and 'Hotel Take over' among enquiry event types, and offers 'Micro weddings at Katikies Hotels in Santorini or Mykonos', described as small, exclusive ceremonies 'featuring classic Cycladic architecture'. Re-check of Greece venues pack fact_300, fact_302: unchanged.

Katikies events page lists four Katikies Mykonos venues: Upper deck (seated 50, standing 100, 'Ideal for wedding ceremonies; private dinners; standing cocktail receptions'); Botrini's Restaurant (seated 50, standing 60); Fleur de Miraval (seated 50, standing 80); Private Balcony (seated 20, standing 20). Only the Upper deck is marked for wedding ceremonies.

Katikies Mykonos describes itself as a 5-star hotel and member of The Leading Hotels of the World 'above the sun kissed beach of Agios Ioannis', about 4 km from Mykonos Town (about a 10-minute drive); all rooms and suites look to Agios Ioannis beach and most have sea views to Delos; children above 13 are welcome (younger children are directed to sister property Katikies Villas Mykonos at Elia beach). Room count is not stated on the page read.

Kivotos (Kivotos Hotels, Mykonos) has an official 'Luxury Weddings in Mykonos' page saying the beachfront hotel 'has a private chapel within its premises', with specialised wedding coordinators handling items from marriage licences to decoration, music and food. The page opens with 'The fairytale like scenery of Cyclades'. Page last modified February 2022.

Kivotos says its most popular wedding reception venue is the entire area around the main pool on the hotel's lower level, against the Aegean backdrop, and offers three named wedding packages (Dreamy Life, Live Life & Love Life, Get Together) that include help with municipal paperwork. Guest capacity, room count and exclusive use are not stated on the page read.

Kivotos Mykonos's home page says the hotel overlooks Ornos Bay, has 40 suites and villas set 'in harmony with nature's handiwork and the classic Cycladic design' down a rocky hillside to its own private beach, reserved for hotel guests and wind-protected, and is a member of L.V.X Preferred Hotels & Resorts.

Kivotos says private meals, intimate gatherings or small cocktail parties can be held by the beach, in a separate private area or on board the hotel's yacht; its weddings page names the hotel's privately owned schooner 'Prince de Neufchatel' as a honeymoon option.

Bill&Coo's 'Celebrations & Events' page (billandcoo.com/retreats) says 'We curate refined luxury weddings and events' under a Weddings & Celebrations heading, calls its venues 'A remarkable backdrop for any celebration, wedding, or event', and offers 'Exclusive Private Events' where couples can host the celebration in one of its venues and accommodate guests in rooms and suites available for private bookings, 'having an entire venue dedicated to your event'. Beefbar Mykonos on Bill&Coo Beach is named as a beachside event venue. Capacities are not stated.

Bill&Coo's home page calls itself 'A love letter to Cyclades', 'overlooking the Aegean Sea', a Leading Hotels of the World member, with three stays: Bill&Coo Mykonos ('a sea view escape near Mykonos Town', where the Valmont Spa is, 'minutes from town'), The Coast Bill&Coo ('intimate seaside retreat') and Private Villas. The LHW member link names Megali Ammos.

The Coast Bill&Coo is described on its own page as 'an intimate, adults-only beachside retreat' on the bay of Agios Ioannis, about seven minutes from Mykonos Town, with 25 suites in 'a subtle homage to authentic Cycladic design' and terraces looking over the Aegean to Delos; its menu links to a separate 'Celebrate' page (billandcoo.com/coast/retreats). Which Bill&Coo property hosts a given wedding is not stated on the pages read.

Rocabella Mykonos: the official site rocabella-hotel-mykonos.com could not be read live (home, contact and stay pages each timed out on 2026-11-11). Only a search snippet of its contact page mentions 'wedding & events inquiries', and a stay page snippet places it about 300 m from Agios Stefanos beach. Under the inclusion rule (live read, never snippets alone) Rocabella does not qualify on this check.

Santa Marina's 2026 wedding brochure PDF (linked from the weddings page) timed out and was not read, so no capacity, room count, ceremony type or exclusive-use detail is recorded from it. Prices in it, if any, are excluded by instruction.

Santa Marina's home page structured data describes it as 'a beachfront retreat on a private peninsula at the southern tip of Ornos Bay, Mykonos', with rooms, suites and villas with Aegean views, infinity pools, a private sandy beach and the Ginkgo Spa, 'just minutes from Mykonos Town'; the resort is marking 40 years. It does not use the word 'Cycladic' on the pages read.

Mykonos Blu (Grecotel) has a 'Weddings & Vow Renewals' page on its official site, with a 'Request for weddings' enquiry option, dedicated wedding specialists, customised menus and trusted vendors. Page modified 21 October 2026.

Mykonos Blu wedding page: 'Extraordinary wedding experiences on the most exclusive beach in Greece, Psarou, with the enchanting sunset as a backdrop'. Highlights listed include 'a Cycladic settlement on the waterfront' and 103 guest rooms.

Mykonos Blu ceremony venue: The Ocean Balcony, 'accommodating up to 60 guests, perched just above the pristine beach of Psarou' with an uninterrupted sea view. After the ceremony the hotel can arrange the wedding table and party for up to 120 guests in its L'Archipel restaurant and pool area. Ceremony type (civil, Orthodox or symbolic) is not stated.

Petasos Beach Resort's official 'Plan an event in Mykonos' page says the resort 'is set on a private peninsula' with a panoramic view of the Aegean, and that its indoor and outdoor venues can contribute to 'a meeting, conference, wedding celebration, or any other type of memorable special event'. Page meta description: 'Weddings, corporate gatherings and private functions handled with care and precision.'

Petasos Beach Resort event facilities table (banquet / reception / cocktail): V.I.P. Restaurant 180 / 220 / 300; Le Club Restaurant 70 / 90 / 110; Swimming Pool 280 / 350 / 500. The page also names The Amphitheatre (no capacity given).

Myconian Ambassador (Relais & Chateaux) has an official 'Weddings & Events' page: 'Exchanging vows in a small chapel, followed by a reception on the beach or our entertainment deck'. Mykonos Blu official homepage: 'Mykonos Blu, Psarou Beach. A Cycladic Icon on the most celebrated beach of the island', with Cycladic architecture, suites and villas with private pools on the Psarou waterfront, and 'The BLU emblematic cave pool'. Structured-data address: Platis Yialos, Mykonos 84600. Room categories include rooms, suites and villas (rooms, suites and private-pool villas); a total room count is not stated on the pages read.

Petasos Beach Resort amenities listed on its official homepage include a two-level saltwater swimming pool with waterfall, the 500 sq m Aqua Marine Spa with thalassotherapy pool, and meeting and banquet rooms. Its event page does not name ceremony types or a ceremony venue.

Myconian Ambassador official homepage: 'Set above Platis Gialos beach ... just 5km away from the vibrant energy of Mykonos Town', with neighbouring Psarou within walking distance. facts.claim: Grecotel Mykonos Lolita's own weddings page (grecotel.com/mykonos-lolita/weddings-mykonos/, modified 22 July 2026) offers 'Religious, civil & symbolic weddings at the hotel's chapel overlooking the deep blue and crystal-clear waters', describes the setting as off the beaten path and close to the island of Delos, and takes enquiries through a request-for-proposal form and the hotel's events email.

Grecotel Mykonos Lolita's homepage says it is 'a little hotel on a secluded private beach after Agios Sostis' (address Agios Sostis, Mykonos 846 00), with 'two whitewashed churches lingering above the Aegean' that 'provide a striking Cycladic setting for weddings and celebrations', a tiny restaurant above a cliff (the Veranda), independent suites and rooms on 2 levels overlooking the Aegean, an infinity pool with hydro massage, and a path down to the beach; it is near Agios Sostis beach and Panormos beach. Grecotel's group wedding page calls the Lolita private chapel 'Pure Cycladic bliss ... with infinite views to the Aegean sea'.
facts.conflicts: The Lolita homepage mentions 'two whitewashed churches'; the weddings page and the Grecotel group page refer to a single chapel ('the hotel's chapel', 'private chapel'). The article should say 'a private chapel' and not state a number of chapels.

facts.claim: Grecotel Mykonos Lolita's accommodation page lists six room and suite types (Classic Room, Classic Room Sea View, Junior Suite, Junior Suite Panoramic Sea View, Superior Suite, Grande Suite 2 Bedrooms), most for 2+1 persons and the Grande Suite for 4 adults, many with views of Panormos Bay, plus a villa, Villa Thea. As at November 2026, Smartraveller's Greece advice (updated 30 September 2026, still current at 11 November 2026) is 'Exercise normal safety precautions' (level green). It says heatwaves are frequent over the summer months and can cause heat exhaustion, heat stroke and death, and that many major tourist sites have little shade.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says wildfires occur in Greece during the extended summer period, from June to September, including near cities and tourist locations, prompting evacuations; fires can start with little warning and travel quickly. It also notes extreme weather throughout the year, including heavy snowfall and flooding in winter, and its latest update advises care when swimming (boat traffic, coastal hazards, strong currents, marine life) and swimming at patrolled beaches where possible.

The Hellenic National Meteorological Service (HNMS/EMY) 'Climatic Data by City' page for the South Aegean lists only Naxos and Rodos as stations; there is no Mykonos station in that table. The hnms.gr address failed a TLS check on 11 November 2026; the page was read at oldportal.emy.gr (HNMS).

Mykonos Airport's official site says a bus service runs between the airport and the city of Mykonos (Chora) and other destinations, from a stop in front of the terminal building (Arrivals area), with tickets bought from the driver (more information at mykonosbus.com); a taxi stand is outside the Arrivals terminal building.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's 'Getting married overseas' page (last updated 18/08/2026, re-checked 11 November 2026, unchanged from corfu-wedding-venues fact_203) says some countries ask you to prove you are free to marry, most commonly with a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) and registry certificates; DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia but some local authorities only accept ones issued in their country, so ask the destination's embassy or consulate whether you need one, whether you can get it in Australia, and whether it needs an authentication or apostille. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says (re-checked 11 November 2026, unchanged from corfu-wedding-venues fact_204) an overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia but in most cases is legally recognised if it was valid under the law of the country where it happened and would have been valid under Australian law had it occurred here; a foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of marriage but may not work as proof of a name change. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, the Australian Embassy in Athens (re-checked 11 November 2026, unchanged from corfu-wedding-venues fact_205) lists among its notarial services witnessing application forms for, and issuing, Certificates of No Impediment (CNI), witnessing notices of intended marriage, and legalisation by authentication or apostille. All notarial services need an appointment (Monday to Friday, 9:00am to 12:30pm), though apostille and CNI documents can be submitted by post; legalised documents and CNIs are ready for collection within two working days unless same-day collection is arranged; the Embassy gives no legal advice, honorary consuls cannot provide notarial services, and fees apply. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

The page does not name the meltemi or give seasonal wind data.

insider_details.detail: Agios Ioannis gives two chapel-led options a short way apart: Mykonos Grand's hilltop chapel holds 25 inside with outdoor ceremonies up to 100, while Katikies Mykonos marks only its Upper deck (seated 50) for ceremonies. Over 50 seated guests points to Mykonos Grand; under 50 suits either.

Mykonos Grand hosts religious ceremonies on its premises only when both partners are Christian Orthodox, so couples planning a civil or symbolic ceremony should confirm in writing which ceremony types each shortlisted venue will host before paying a deposit.

Ornos Bay holds two very different scales: Santa Marina is a full resort on its own peninsula with a stone chapel and in-house wedding planners, while Kivotos has 40 suites and villas, its own chapel and a pool-level reception area, a natural fit for a smaller wedding where most guests stay on site.

Several venues set age limits that matter for family weddings: Katikies Mykonos welcomes children over 13 only and The Coast Bill&Coo is adults-only, so couples with young nieces and nephews on the guest list need a room-block plan that includes a family-friendly property.

Bill&Coo is the clearest option in this batch for a private, whole-venue celebration: it states that guests can be accommodated in rooms and suites booked privately with 'an entire venue dedicated to your event'. The Coast has 25 suites, so check how many guests that houses before treating it as exclusive use.

At Mykonos Blu the ceremony space and the reception space are sized differently: The Ocean Balcony holds up to 60 for the ceremony, while L'Archipel restaurant and the pool area take up to 120 for dinner and dancing, so a guest list between 61 and 120 needs a conversation with the hotel about where the vows can happen.

Petasos Beach Resort publishes the largest numbers in this batch: its pool area seats 280 at a banquet (500 for cocktails) and the V.I.P. Restaurant seats 180, which makes it the Platis Gialos option for a bigger guest list, but its event page names no ceremony spot, so ask the Wedded Advisor to confirm where the vows themselves would take place.

Myconian Ambassador is the intimate choice of the Myconian Collection: its own wedding page pairs a small chapel with a beach or deck reception and sends grand banquets to the group's Elia hotels, so couples planning a large celebration should compare it with the Elia properties rather than book it for scale.

Psarou and Platis Gialos sit side by side: Petasos describes itself as on a peninsula between the two beaches, and the Ambassador says Psarou is within walking distance, so a couple could base guests across these hotels without a long transfer between them.

Soho Roc House at Paraga says on its own page that it sits among lively beach clubs where music can be energetic, which matters for a sunset chapel ceremony; plan the ceremony time and sound expectations in writing with the Wedded Advisor before committing.

Only one venue in this batch publishes a seated number: the Myconian Collection's Horizons Ballroom takes 270 at round tables or 380 to 400 banquet style, so it suits the larger end of a 40 to 150 guest list; for Mykonos Lolita and Ftelia Bay, get the chapel and reception capacity in writing before shortlisting.

The Myconian Collection's own fleet runs 15-seat minibuses and 40-seat mini-coaches, so a 120-guest wedding moves in about three coach loads; plan the timeline around that before the ceremony time is fixed.

Royal Myconian and Myconian Imperial share one wedding text and one events team with the wider collection, so enquire once through the collection's weddings page and ask which hotel's chapel, beach and ballroom your date would use, rather than comparing the two hotels as separate venues.

Mykonos Lolita's rooms are mostly for 2+1 guests with one 2-bedroom Grande Suite and a villa, and it is a small hotel on a secluded beach beyond Agios Sostis, so expect to house part of a larger guest list elsewhere; ask whether a full-hotel booking is possible on your dates.

Mykonos Lolita states religious, civil and symbolic ceremonies at its chapel, which makes it one of the few venues here where the ceremony type is published; the Myconian Collection says only that it assists with ceremonies of all denominations.

Myconian Villa Collection's weddings offer sits with the wider Myconian Collection events team, so ask early which of the group's venues and restaurants would host the ceremony and the reception, and get capacity and room numbers in writing, as none are published on the Villa Collection pages.

Mykonos Airport's official site lists only a public bus from in front of Arrivals and a taxi stand outside the terminal, so for a wedding group plan pre-booked private coach or car transfers rather than relying on the rank.

Smartraveller warns of frequent summer heatwaves and of wildfires from June to September; for a July or August wedding, schedule the ceremony late in the day, plan shade and water for guests, and keep the guest list contactable in case of local fire advice.

Mykonos is a short domestic hop from Athens (about 45 minutes, per Visit Greece), so couples needing a CNI or apostille from the Australian Embassy in Athens can fit an appointment (weekdays, 9:00am to 12:30pm) around a stopover; CNIs and apostilles are ready within two working days unless same-day collection is arranged.

Saint John sits in Agios Ioannis, which the hotel calls one of Mykonos' most iconic sunset spots, and offers three ceremony spots (Agia Fotini Chapel, the sunset balcony, the deck). Time the ceremony to the sunset and keep the outdoor spots for the vows, with an indoor reception room (Ilios or Thalatta) as the weather backup.

ZeNIT is an events-only venue on a hill above Paradise beach with no guest rooms, so couples need a separate hotel block and a transfer plan. The venue itself only runs transfers for up to 16 guests, with larger groups through partners or by sea on the Phoebus boat; book coaches early for a full guest list.
ZeNIT's central indoor hall is its stated all-weather option, so plan it as the wet-weather or windy-day fallback and confirm how the hall and terraces are split between ceremony and dinner.

open_questions.question: Batch A qualifies 5: Santa Marina, Katikies Mykonos, Mykonos Grand (all candidates) plus reserves Kivotos Mykonos and Bill&Coo. Belvedere fails (no weddings offer); Rocabella not readable (three timeouts, snippets only). No Mykonos Town venue qualified except Bill&Coo Mykonos at Megali Ammos on the Town edge; no Agios Stefanos venue qualified.

Batch B qualified 4 of 5: Mykonos Blu (Psarou), Petasos Beach Resort (Platis Gialos), Myconian Ambassador (Platis Gialos) and Soho Roc House, formerly San Giorgio (Paraga). Kensho Psarou excluded (fact_112). Soho Roc House is a members' club closed until spring 2027: include it or hold it as a reserve?
Mykonos Blu and Soho Roc House are closed for the 2026 to 2027 winter; confirm 2027 opening dates before any date-led copy (verify_items).

Batch C qualifies 2 venues (Myconian Collection at Elia as ONE entry, Grecotel Mykonos Lolita) plus Ftelia Bay Hotel as a conditional reserve. Royal Myconian and Myconian Imperial are not separate wedding venues. Pietra e Mare fails the inclusion rule. Kalo Livadi and Houlakia have no qualifying venue.

Batch D qualifies 1 venue: Myconian Villa Collection (Elia Beach, south coast), whose official site has a Weddings and Events page. Villa Joy Mykonos (villajoymykonos.com, Ano Mera) does NOT qualify: its official pages offer retreats and 'Events & Shootings' but never say weddings (a second domain, mykonosexclusivevilla.com, failed TLS). No other villa estate or event venue with its own official weddings page was found: search returned directories, rental agents and social posts only (Villa Almi, Mykonos Rocks, Alia leads have no official site read). Saint John Mykonos (saintjohn.gr) has a weddings blog mentioning a private whitewashed chapel; it is a hotel, not in this batch's scope, and was not read.

Batch E qualifies 3 venues: Saint John Hotel Villas & Spa (Agios Ioannis, fact_400 to fact_402), ZeNIT Events Center (Paradise beach, events-only venue with no rooms, fact_405 to fact_407) and Semeli Hotel Mykonos (Mykonos Town, weaker: 2020 blog post only, fact_403 and fact_404). Failed: Kouros Hotel & Suites (no weddings page), Cavo Tagoo (weddings named for Santorini only), Mykonos Theoxenia (privacy statement only), Lyo Mykonos (no official site result), Kalesma (search timed out, not retried).
